# core: Fields

Part of [core](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core), PocketBase's Go package `core` as JavaScript sees it. The same types in Go: [core: Fields](/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/core/fields).

## core.FieldFactoryFunc

FieldFactoryFunc defines a simple function to construct a specific Field instance.

## core.Field

Field defines a common interface that all Collection fields should implement.

## core.AutodateField

AutodateField defines an "autodate" type field, aka.
field which datetime value could be auto set on record create/update.

This field is usually used for defining timestamp fields like "created" and "updated".

Requires either both or at least one of the OnCreate or OnUpdate options to be set.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> | Name (required) is the unique name of the field. |
| `id` | <code>string</code> | Id is the unique stable field identifier. |
| `system` | <code>boolean</code> | System prevents the renaming and removal of the field. |
| `hidden` | <code>boolean</code> | Hidden hides the field from the API response. |
| `presentable` | <code>boolean</code> | Presentable hints the Dashboard UI to use the underlying field record value in the relation preview label. |
| `onCreate` | <code>boolean</code> | OnCreate auto sets the current datetime as field value on record create. |
| `onUpdate` | <code>boolean</code> | OnUpdate auto sets the current datetime as field value on record update. |

## core.FileField

FileField defines "file" type field for managing record file(s).

Only the file name is stored as part of the record value.
New files (aka. files to upload) are expected to be of *filesystem.File.

If MaxSelect is not set or <= 1, then the field value is expected to be a single record id.

If MaxSelect is > 1, then the field value is expected to be a slice of record ids.

The respective zero record field value is either empty string (single) or empty string slice (multiple).

---

The following additional setter keys are available:

```
  - "fieldName+" - append one or more files to the existing record one. For example:

    // []string{"old1.txt", "old2.txt", "new1_ajkvass.txt", "new2_klhfnwd.txt"}
    record.Set("documents+", []*filesystem.File{new1, new2})

  - "+fieldName" - prepend one or more files to the existing record one. For example:

    // []string{"new1_ajkvass.txt", "new2_klhfnwd.txt", "old1.txt", "old2.txt",}
    record.Set("+documents", []*filesystem.File{new1, new2})

  - "fieldName-" - subtract/delete one or more files from the existing record one. For example:

    // []string{"old2.txt",}
    record.Set("documents-", "old1.txt")
```

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> | Name (required) is the unique name of the field. |
| `id` | <code>string</code> | Id is the unique stable field identifier. |
| `system` | <code>boolean</code> | System prevents the renaming and removal of the field. |
| `hidden` | <code>boolean</code> | Hidden hides the field from the API response. |
| `presentable` | <code>boolean</code> | Presentable hints the Dashboard UI to use the underlying field record value in the relation preview label. |
| `help` | <code>string</code> | Help is an extra text explaining what the field is about. It is usually shown in Dashboard UI under the field input. |
| `maxSize` | <code>number</code> | MaxSize specifies the maximum size of a single uploaded file (in bytes and up to 2^53-1). |
| `maxSelect` | <code>number</code> | MaxSelect specifies the max allowed files. |
| `mimeTypes` | <code>Array&lt;string&gt;</code> | MimeTypes specifies an optional list of the allowed file mime types. |
| `thumbs` | <code>Array&lt;string&gt;</code> | Thumbs specifies an optional list of the supported thumbs for image based files. |
| `protected` | <code>boolean</code> | Protected will require the users to provide a special file token to access the file. |
| `required` | <code>boolean</code> | Required will require the field value to have at least one file. |

## core.GeoPointField

GeoPointField defines "geoPoint" type field for storing latitude and longitude GPS coordinates.

You can set the record field value as [`types.geoPoint`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/types#typesgeopoint), map or serialized json object with lat-lon props.
The stored value is always converted to [`types.geoPoint`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/types#typesgeopoint).
Nil, empty map, empty bytes slice, etc. results in zero [`types.geoPoint`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/types#typesgeopoint).

Examples of updating a record's GeoPointField value programmatically:

```
	record.Set("location", types.GeoPoint{Lat: 123, Lon: 456})
	record.Set("location", map[string]any{"lat":123, "lon":456})
	record.Set("location", []byte(`{"lat":123, "lon":456}`)
```

## core.NumberField

NumberField defines "number" type field for storing numeric (float64) value.

The respective zero record field value is 0.

The following additional setter keys are available:

```
  - "fieldName+" - appends to the existing record value. For example:
    record.Set("total+", 5)
  - "fieldName-" - subtracts from the existing record value. For example:
    record.Set("total-", 5)
```

## core.PasswordField

PasswordField defines "password" type field for storing bcrypt hashed strings
(usually used only internally for the "password" auth collection system field).

If you want to set a direct bcrypt hash as record field value you can use the SetRaw method, for example:

```
	// generates a bcrypt hash of "123456" and set it as field value
	// (record.GetString("password") returns the plain password until persisted, otherwise empty string)
	record.Set("password", "123456")

	// set directly a bcrypt hash of "123456" as field value
	// (record.GetString("password") returns empty string)
	record.SetRaw("password", "$2a$10$.5Elh8fgxypNUWhpUUr/xOa2sZm0VIaE0qWuGGl9otUfobb46T1Pq")
```

The following additional getter keys are available:

```
  - "fieldName:hash" - returns the bcrypt hash string of the record field value (if any). For example:
    record.GetString("password:hash")
```

## core.RelationField

RelationField defines "relation" type field for storing single or
multiple collection record references.

Requires the CollectionId option to be set.

If MaxSelect is not set or <= 1, then the field value is expected to be a single record id.

If MaxSelect is > 1, then the field value is expected to be a slice of record ids.

The respective zero record field value is either empty string (single) or empty string slice (multiple).

---

The following additional setter keys are available:

```
  - "fieldName+" - append one or more values to the existing record one. For example:

    record.Set("categories+", []string{"new1", "new2"}) // []string{"old1", "old2", "new1", "new2"}

  - "+fieldName" - prepend one or more values to the existing record one. For example:

    record.Set("+categories", []string{"new1", "new2"}) // []string{"new1", "new2", "old1", "old2"}

  - "fieldName-" - subtract one or more values from the existing record one. For example:

    record.Set("categories-", "old1") // []string{"old2"}
```

|---|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> | Name (required) is the unique name of the field. |
| `id` | <code>string</code> | Id is the unique stable field identifier. |

## core.SelectField

SelectField defines "select" type field for storing single or
multiple string values from a predefined list.

Requires the Values option to be set.

If MaxSelect is not set or <= 1, then the field value is expected to be a single Values element.

If MaxSelect is > 1, then the field value is expected to be a subset of Values slice.

The respective zero record field value is either empty string (single) or empty string slice (multiple).

---

The following additional setter keys are available:

```
  - "fieldName+" - append one or more values to the existing record one. For example:

    record.Set("roles+", []string{"new1", "new2"}) // []string{"old1", "old2", "new1", "new2"}

  - "+fieldName" - prepend one or more values to the existing record one. For example:

    record.Set("+roles", []string{"new1", "new2"}) // []string{"new1", "new2", "old1", "old2"}

  - "fieldName-" - subtract one or more values from the existing record one. For example:

    record.Set("roles-", "old1") // []string{"old2"}
```

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> | Name (required) is the unique name of the field. |
| `id` | <code>string</code> | Id is the unique stable field identifier. |
| `system` | <code>boolean</code> | System prevents the renaming and removal of the field. |
| `hidden` | <code>boolean</code> | Hidden hides the field from the API response. |
| `presentable` | <code>boolean</code> | Presentable hints the Dashboard UI to use the underlying field record value in the relation preview label. |
| `help` | <code>string</code> | Help is an extra text explaining what the field is about. It is usually shown in Dashboard UI under the field input. |
| `values` | <code>Array&lt;string&gt;</code> | Values specifies the list of accepted values. |
| `maxSelect` | <code>number</code> | MaxSelect specifies the max allowed selected values. |
| `required` | <code>boolean</code> | Required will require the field value to be non-empty. |

## core.TextField

TextField defines "text" type field for storing any string value.

The respective zero record field value is empty string.

The following additional setter keys are available:

- "fieldName:autogenerate" - autogenerate field value if AutogeneratePattern is set. For example:

```
	record.Set("slug:autogenerate", "") // [random value]
	record.Set("slug:autogenerate", "abc-") // abc-[random value]
```

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> | Name (required) is the unique name of the field. |
| `id` | <code>string</code> | Id is the unique stable field identifier. |
| `system` | <code>boolean</code> | System prevents the renaming and removal of the field. |
| `hidden` | <code>boolean</code> | Hidden hides the field from the API response. |
| `presentable` | <code>boolean</code> | Presentable hints the Dashboard UI to use the underlying field record value in the relation preview label. |
| `help` | <code>string</code> | Help is an extra text explaining what the field is about. It is usually shown in Dashboard UI under the field input. |
| `min` | <code>number</code> | Min specifies the minimum required string characters. |
| `max` | <code>number</code> | Max specifies the maximum allowed string characters. |
| `pattern` | <code>string</code> | Pattern specifies an optional regex pattern to match against the field value. |
| `autogeneratePattern` | <code>string</code> | AutogeneratePattern specifies an optional regex pattern that could be used to generate random string from it and set it automatically on record create if no explicit value is set or when the `:autogenerate` modifier is used. |
| `required` | <code>boolean</code> | Required will require the field value to be non-empty string. |
| `primaryKey` | <code>boolean</code> | PrimaryKey will mark the field as primary key. |
| `type()` | <code>(): string</code> | Type implements [`Field.type`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/fields#corefield) interface method. |

| `setName()` | <code>(name: string): void</code> | SetName implements [`Field.setName`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/fields#corefield) interface method. |
| `getSystem()` | <code>(): boolean</code> | GetSystem implements [`Field.getSystem`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/fields#corefield) interface method. |
| `setSystem()` | <code>(system: boolean): void</code> | SetSystem implements [`Field.setSystem`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/fields#corefield) interface method. |

## core.FieldsList

FieldsList defines a Collection slice of fields.

Has everything <code>Array&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/fields#corefield">Field</a>&gt;</code> has.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `clone()` | <code>(): <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/fields#corefieldslist">FieldsList</a></code> | Clone creates a deep clone of the current list. |
| `fieldNames()` | <code>(): Array&lt;string&gt;</code> | FieldNames returns a slice with the name of all list fields. |
| `asMap()` | <code>(): { [key: string]: any }</code> | AsMap returns a map with all registered list field. The returned map is indexed with each field name. |
| `getById()` | <code>(fieldId: string): <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/fields#corefield">Field</a></code> | GetById returns a single field by its id. |
| `getByName()` | <code>(fieldName: string): <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/fields#corefield">Field</a></code> | GetByName returns a single field by its name. |
| `removeById()` | <code>(fieldId: string): void</code> | RemoveById removes a single field by its id. |
| `removeByName()` | <code>(fieldName: string): void</code> | RemoveByName removes a single field by its name. |
| `add()` | <code>(...fields: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/fields#corefield">Field</a>[]): void</code> | Add adds one or more fields to the current list. |
| `addAt()` | <code>(pos: number, ...fields: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/fields#corefield">Field</a>[]): void</code> | AddAt is the same as Add but insert/move the fields at the specific position. |
| `addMarshaledJSON()` | <code>(rawJSON: string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;): void</code> | AddMarshaledJSON parses the provided raw json data and adds the found fields into the current list (following the same rule as the Add method). |
| `addMarshaledJSONAt()` | <code>(pos: number, rawJSON: string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;): void</code> | AddMarshaledJSONAt is the same as AddMarshaledJSON but insert/move the fields at the specific position. |
| `string()` | <code>(): string</code> | String returns the string representation of the current list. |
| `unmarshalJSON()` | <code>(data: string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;): void</code> | UnmarshalJSON implements `json.unmarshaler` and loads the provided json data into the current FieldsList. |
| `marshalJSON()` | <code>(): string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;</code> | MarshalJSON implements the `json.marshaler` interface. |
| `value()` | <code>(): any</code> | Value implements the `driver.valuer` interface. |
| `scan()` | <code>(value: any): void</code> | Scan implements `sql.scanner` interface to scan the provided value into the current FieldsList instance. |
